stemMd: A jar contains 4 red capsules and 2 white capsules, identical apart from colour. Two capsules are drawn at random, one after the other, without putting the first back. What is the probability that the two capsules are the same colour?
explanationMd:
**What to notice first.** \"Same colour\" means two red **or** two white: two disjoint cases whose probabilities add.

**The computation.** Two red: $\tfrac46\cdot\tfrac35=\tfrac{12}{30}=\tfrac{6}{15}$. Two white: $\tfrac26\cdot\tfrac15=\tfrac{2}{30}=\tfrac{1}{15}$. Total: $\tfrac{6}{15}+\tfrac{1}{15}=\tfrac{7}{15}$.

**How to check it.** Count unordered pairs: there are $\binom{6}{2}=15$ pairs in all, $\binom{4}{2}=6$ red pairs and $\binom{2}{2}=1$ white pair, so $\tfrac{7}{15}$ again. The complement, one of each colour, is $\tfrac{4\cdot 2}{15}=\tfrac{8}{15}$, and $\tfrac{7}{15}+\tfrac{8}{15}=1$.

distractorRationale.b: Counts only the two-red case, $\tfrac{6}{15}$, and forgets that two white capsules are also the same colour.
distractorRationale.e: Treats the draws as if the first capsule were put back: $\left(\tfrac46\right)^{2}+\left(\tfrac26\right)^{2}=\tfrac{20}{36}$.
distractorRationale.d: Computes the probability of one capsule of each colour, the complement of the event asked for.
distractorRationale.a: Counts only the two-white case and forgets the much more likely two-red case.

accessibilityText: A jar has 4 red and 2 white capsules. Two are drawn at random without replacement. Find the probability that both are the same colour. The five choices are: two fifths; five ninths; seven fifteenths; eight fifteenths; one fifteenth.

provenance.notes: Original item on drawing without replacement with a union of two disjoint cases. Distractors: one case only (either colour), drawing with replacement, and the complementary event.

review.author: tolc-f-wave8-mpl-author

independentSolve.workingNotes: P = (4/6)(3/5) + (2/6)(1/5) = 12/30 + 2/30 = 7/15. 2/5 is red-red only; 1/15 is white-white only; 8/15 is the complement (different colours); 5/9 uses replacement. [A second, separate blind solve (blind-reviewer-wave8-tolcf-mpl-run1) reached the same answer: P(RR)+P(WW) = (4/6)(3/5)+(2/6)(1/5) = 12/30+2/30 = 7/15. 2/5 is RR only, 1/15 is WW only, 8/15 is the probability of different colours, 5/9 is with replacement.]
